Senses.Explanation: The true eye at the crown is an emphatic image for the capacity to discern and respond without being trapped by the presented terms. Yongzhang Jun and Fuxin Bencai say that it must be opened or that everyone has it; a preface praises Hanxiu Ruqian as possessing it; other records test it in questions about light and the teaching seat. Zen relocates “seeing” to the crown of the head to mark an examiner’s decisive vision, not an anatomical organ.
